Anthony Fenech
Tigers beat writer
Detroit Free Press
(734) 752-9667
Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: Sipple, George <gsipple@freepress.com>
Sent: Sunday, December 6, 2015 8:51 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Subject: al quotes 
 
“What we’re trying to do is keep our young pitching. This winter, everybody asked for them. I mean guys like Fulmer, Norris and even Boyd. Those were the three guys that people talked about all the time. Now in saying that, there were other guys a little bit younger that were asked about too within the system. I can tell you that we did everything in our power to keep them. Every move that you see us make has been for us, to put the best team on the field for ’16, but also looking toward the future as best we can. I think I’ve also told you, one of my beliefs as far as trying to win this year is quality depth in pitching. You’re going to need more than the five starters.
“We feel this year, we have quality arms that when we need a starter or need a reliever, we’re going to have a quality arm to come up and be a lot better than we had last year.
And those same guys will then in the future step in and take some spots.

In addition to that, we’re going to try to develop one, maybe two guys, into a backend bullpen guy. And hopefully a closer-type guy. That if we needed somebody like that this season, we’re going to try to get a guy ready for that job and then maybe in the future, in the following years.
Rondon? It could be rondon. But now we have other guys. Now it’s not just Rondon. It’s like Rondon plus.
Winter league?
Actually Valdez has done well so far.
Joe Jimenez?

That will be determined in spring training. My hope, personal hope, is that he ends up in Double-A. In saying that, we’ve pushed guys a little bit, maybe faster than we would want in the past. It’ll be determined in spring training. I would say that if he goes to Double-A, I will be assured that he will have success.”
(Avila told a story that calling David Chadd up about Christin Stewart, the young power hitter they drafted last season out of Tennessee)
“I assured you,” Chadd said.
“He says, we gotta take him to West Michigan,” Avila said. “I said, ‘no we’re not.’ We’re not pushing guys. I said, Can he hit there?’ (Chadd) was right.”
Chadd then said: “That’s the PG version….that’s the mild version.”
On analytics
“I can’t throw them under the bud. From an analystics department, I can’t tell you they wanted ‘Hey, go get Pelfrey.’
Jay: There’s things we like about Pelfrey too. I’m not a person that works in absolutes. There are skills that he has that are absolutely positive that we saw.
We service that information, as we service all the information to Al, to make a collaborative decision. We don’t have all of the answers and we understand that.
Is there a profile of what a Tiger pitcher needs to do from a an analtics standpoint?
Jay: “Analystically, there is no idea. You’re trying to look for a pitcher that has positive results in the field. How  you get to those results can happen in vastly different manners.
An example to gauage future performance?

“I won’t go into details, but it’s exhausitive. We’re trying o look at every piece of information that we can have an analyze. There are things obviously that we find that are more important….Even people within the department find to be better predictors, but I wouldn’t go into what the specifics are.”

Al: “They have even disagreed. Or have difference of opinions on certain players. You talk to Jay and Sam and Koo. They’ll have opinions on diferent players and their opinions are different based on their own numbers. Not too different than scouts would have different opinions on a player.
There’s a lot of information. It’s about putting it all together and making one good decisions. People can skew that information.

Back in the old days, there would run up a report that was so convincing that man, I have to have that player. They loved that player. They wrote it up in a way that made you go that way. It can happen too with the numbers. You can skew the numbers to make the player look more attractive.
Scout sign: “In this case, yeah, Im not going to throw them under the bus. This Is more a scout signing.”
On beefing up analytics:

Al: “It has changed it completely. Yes. I’ve talked to Sam and Jay and I’ve said, any time we have meetings or we talk about players, acquisition of players or trading players, they’re to be in that meeting no matter what. They are part of that meeting as if they are anybody else here, whether that be Scott Bream, David Chadd, Al Kaline. They’re in that room with as much authority as anybody there, with as much say. And we take it all to heart. Now, that doesn’t mean we’re going to make decisions based only on that. The pelfrey thing tells you exactly what we just did.”
I don’t even know what they do to tell you the truth.

We just get the numbers, we get the rankings. It’s very complicated and they are working at it hours and hours and hours. It’s a lot of work and other teams will tell you – and I’ve dealt with other teams in trades and it takes them a while to get through all the numbers. They’ll come back, here’s the offer, take it or leave it. We do the same thing.
George Sipple
Detroit Free Press
@GeorgeSipple
